independentAdversarial.meaning: Assertions preserve observed counterexamples; exit0 is not candidate acceptance

notRunByReviewer: inputs.test.js (creates markers outside assigned reviewer write roots)
controller.test.js (default real host marker outside reviewer ownership)

findings.title: Physical consumed inputs and profile can change while DRIFT and publication still PASS
findings.expected: SPEC lines 229–259, 307–309, 322–325, 403–409: retain/verify exact consumed bytes before native execution and after cleanup; changed frozen profile is DRIFT_RUNTIME/INFRA_FAILURE.

code.detail: Only bundle-source copies and their originals become retained pins.
Bundle inventory, separate stdin, mounted workspace settings/MCP, consumed inventory and empty directory are created without retained pins/inventory verification.
Profile is persisted but never pinned.
DRIFT checks original manifest plus context.pins and claims mounted snapshots match.
Publication validator receives evidence.retained memory, not current artifact bytes.

findings.reproduction: Before simulated START_NATIVE, overwrite each of mounted settings, mounted MCP, profile, consumed-inputs, bundle-inventory and separately retained stdin in six independent owned runs. Each returns PORT_OBSERVED/0, all checks PASS, no failures, and a published digest differing from physical bytes. Adding an unlisted file to the supposedly empty readonly volume directory also passes.
findings.impact: Current code can launch against changed mounted settings/MCP and publish a successful immutable-looking report whose retained artifacts disagree with disk. This is the ordinary drift model explicitly required by the SPEC; it does not assume malicious root or modifying candidate source.
findings.correction: Retain descriptor/path/content identity for all physical consumed artifacts, profile and the empty bind inventory. Verify before START_NATIVE and after cleanup; recompute staged evidence from anchored physical bytes before publication. Preserve actual drift as INFRA_FAILURE and never emit a complete successful report.

findings.title: Host SIGINT/SIGTERM use default termination instead of bounded cleanup
findings.expected: SPEC lines 169–174, 373–381: controller cancellation attempts finite cleanup and preserves cause/owned identities; only SIGKILL/power loss lack this guarantee.

code.detail: execute owns lifecycle but installs no SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers or cancellation mechanism.
cleanup is reached only by normal async control flow.
CLI awaits runProbe without signal interception.

findings.reproduction: Own Node22 subprocesses run the real controller with an entirely in-memory Engine, fake toolchain pins and fake marker. At START_PORT both signal listener counts are zero and two virtual resources exist. Self-delivered SIGINT/SIGTERM terminate with the respective signal; intents survive but no cleanup.json or report is written. Parent deadline is 2 seconds.
findings.impact: A routine host cancellation leaves actual owned containers/marker unreconciled until an external operator acts. Wrapper signal handlers do not substitute for host cancellation.
findings.correction: Install scoped host cancellation handlers before side effects, record SIGNAL, stop future starts and route cancellation through one finite cleanup path. Remove handlers in finalization; preserve original cancellation and any cleanup failure. Test both signals with an owned simulated subprocess.

findings.title: Evidence validator accepts rehashed contradictory containment proofs
findings.expected: SPEC lines 397–409 require real proof for every PASS and a validator rejecting omitted/contradictory bindings, not just digest consistency.

code.detail: assertEvidenceBindings checks byte hashes and selected relationships but does not revalidate inspect/preflight security facts.
Trace validation covers frame shape and native hashes, not equivalence of preflight/inspect/profile PASS evidence.
Checks require a valid existing artifact reference, not a proof appropriate to that check.

findings.reproduction: Clone the baseline report and retained bytes in memory. Change a retained inspect HostConfig.Privileged to true; separately change preflight uid to 0, hostMarkerAbsent to false and pidNamespace to the synthetic host inode. Update each artifact bytes/hash. assertEvidenceBindings accepts both reports with PORT_OBSERVED and all containment checks PASS.
findings.impact: A hash-consistent artifact set can contradict its own containment claims and still be accepted by the shipped evidence validator. This is not a claim that an arbitrary attacker can rewrite host evidence; it is a demonstrated SPEC-required verifier failure.
findings.correction: Recompute every required check from its appropriate retained proofs, cardinalities and trace relationships; rerun closed profile/inspect/namespace/preflight equivalence validation and reject any contradiction. Do not weaken the qualified helpers.

findings.title: Nonzero wrapper status aborts removal of an otherwise proven owned container
findings.expected: SPEC lines 373–381 require stop/remove/final absence confirmation for each known owned identity, preserving execution and cleanup errors separately.

code.detail: An exited wrapper with nonzero ExitCode throws IO before reaching rm/final inspect.
Catch leaves the identity UNRESOLVED, although no remove was attempted and daemon is available.

findings.reproduction: After the simulated client STOP/CLOSED, set its actual inspect State.ExitCode to 1. Controller returns INFRA_FAILURE and preserves the failure, but never sends rm for the client and leaves one virtual container; observer removal succeeds.
findings.impact: An abnormal wrapper exit deliberately produces an avoidable resource leak. Failure status and a handoff are honest but do not discharge the required cleanup attempt.
findings.correction: Record the nonzero wrapper observation as an execution failure and continue identity-checked removal/final inspect. Keep execution and cleanup failures separate; only actual inability to reconcile/remove justifies UNRESOLVED.

findings.title: Complete body framing without its trusted REQUEST/RESPONSE is classified as clean absence
findings.expected: SPEC lines 291–299, 339–343, 391–409: missing protected control/body relationships are protocol failure; clean absence requires otherwise intact controls.

code.detail: Wait checks only requests already present in the map; it is vacuously satisfied for orphan body frames.
EOF validates binary framing/terminals but not required matching protected control events.
Orphan terminal bodies become partialBodies while the run can retain intact PHASES/PRIVACY_CAPS.

findings.reproduction: Keep the complete eligible synthetic body and its terminal but suppress its REQUEST and RESPONSE controls, leaving seq contiguous and EOF/CLOSED otherwise valid. Real controller publishes PORT_NOT_OBSERVED with PHASES=PASS and PRIVACY_CAPS=PASS instead of INFRA_FAILURE.
findings.impact: Missing-control evidence is mislabeled as an intact run with no eligible exchange. It does not produce PORT_OBSERVED in this reproducer but violates required incomplete/error observability.
findings.correction: Before intact classification, require a bijection between eligible body ordinal/terminal and protected REQUEST/RESPONSE records, with all required fields/digests/phase/window checked. Preserve orphan bytes as partial failure.

findings.title: Host consumes original source imports; reviewed builtin allowlist is absent from profile
findings.expected: SPEC lines 224–231 requires consuming only the private source/input snapshot and including a fixed Node builtin allowlist in the profile.

code.detail: Host controller is imported from original checkout before snapshot creation.
Its host helper closure is statically imported from original files.
Later snapshot copies the closure but host continues using the original module graph.
Resolved profile has no builtin allowlist.

findings.reproduction: Independent Acorn AST inventory agrees with the Lead: 19 source paths, 214909 bytes, 12 builtins, zero unresolved literal imports/dynamic imports. However inspect the CLI import and profile key list: container wrappers use the copy, host does not; profile omits the reviewed allowlist.
findings.impact: Literal closure completeness is positive evidence but cannot stand in for the approved consumed-source/profile contract. The current result binds copied bytes rather than the entire module graph actually used by the host.
findings.correction: Use a minimal trusted bootstrap to freeze and verify the closure before executing the snapshotted host controller; persist the fixed reviewed builtin allowlist in the approved profile representation. Resolve any schema ambiguity explicitly rather than silently claiming compliance.

compatibilityQuestions.question: Fifth HTTP attempt cannot use ordinal4
compatibilityQuestions.explanation: The closed domain remains 0–3. The observer fails CAP privately and exits nonzero without inventing an ordinal/frame. A protected premature EOF is sufficient to reject the run as incomplete INFRA_FAILURE; it is not sufficient to assert that CAP specifically was observed on the host. Synthetic observer_cap_eof confirms a prior valid exchange does not rescue the result. Actual fifth request cap/exit/cleanup positive control remains NOT_RUN. R1-04 requires avoiding leaks on nonzero cleanup observations.

compatibilityQuestions.question: Local Enginev1.51 HTTP101 attach handshake ≤2s versus observation ≤30s
compatibilityQuestions.explanation: It is coherent to apply the per-call deadline to establishing a counted attach stream, then bound observation by the shared controller deadline. DockerTransport.budget counts attach within 24 calls; handshake has <=2s timer; observation ends at the same global deadline. This does not extend a Docker CLI command to 30s. Fixed local socket/config and preflight API-range refusal are present. No network lookup was performed and no Engine compatibility/101 lifetime was exercised; current image/API availability and final positive controls are NOT_RUN. This judgment follows the approved observation design and inspected source, not a claim that official reference pages were fetched.

compatibilityQuestions.question: Zero-length binary terminal per phase/channel/body; interleaving and EOF
compatibilityQuestions.explanation: Length zero is already admitted by the length domain, so it can unambiguously designate one terminal without adding a wire type/schema. Decoder checks duplicates, data after terminal, malformed/partial EOF; native classification joins actual END and both channel terminals. Byte-fragmentation/terminal safe tests passed. However the observer body/control join is not total: terminal body without REQUEST/RESPONSE is accepted as clean PORT_NOT_OBSERVED (R1-05). Thus the proposed representation is compatible, but strict missing-event/EOF safety is not satisfied by this candidate.

compatibilityQuestions.question: Conservatively exclude observer events/bytes received after host STOP; no invented cross-pipe order
compatibilityQuestions.explanation: Both native START/port and HTTP proof must exist within authorized host START_PORT→STOP; their arrival order need not match across pipes. Observer REQUEST/RESPONSE and raw handlers reject outside that window. Excluding late arrivals may turn an otherwise valid exchange into INFRA_FAILURE (false negative), but cannot manufacture a positive exchange. Synthetic observer_raw_after_stop confirms rejection plus cleanup of both virtual identities. Real pipe scheduling is NOT_RUN. Missing orphan joins and host cancellation/cleanup findings remain independent and must be fixed.

limitations: All Engine/preflight/native/HTTP stimuli in the adversarial integration tests are explicitly simulated.
Physical current Node/Docker/Claude bytes match fixed pins; Docker image/API runtime compatibility is NOT_RUN.
No official web references fetched because network is forbidden in this review.
Lead current full certification is a disjoint live job; no result is inferred and it was not inspected/controlled.
No claim of release, M1, complete functional catalog acceptance or final NP acceptance.
nextAction: Lead preserves/stops only its owned certification attempt, corrects mandatory findings in an authorized correction round, refreezes/reviews current source and evidence, then reissues appropriate gates before any bounded native launch.
